subject: Nonnumeric quoting as a typed round trip between writer and reader
brief:
Make nonnumeric quoting a real round trip between the tabula writer and reader, so that value types survive.

1. `read_rows` and `read_table` take `quoting` (default `minimal`, which keeps today's behavior: every field is text) and the keyword arguments `true` and `false`, the boolean words (by default the words true and false). The only other accepted quoting is `nonnumeric`; any other value raises ValueError.
2. With nonnumeric quoting, whether a field was quoted decides its type. A quoted field is always text, exactly as written, even when it looks like a number or a boolean word, and a quoted field with nothing inside is the empty string. An unquoted field that is empty is missing (None), so the two must not be confused. An unquoted field equal to the true or false word (exact, case-sensitive) is the matching boolean. An unquoted whole number (digits with an optional leading minus) is an int; an unquoted decimal number (digits with a point, or starting with a point, and/or with an exponent, optional leading minus) is a float. Edge case: anything else unquoted is an error, not text: a ParseError carrying the line of the text on which that field stands (line breaks inside quoted fields count, so this is not the row's position). This includes words, numbers with surrounding spaces, a plus sign, underscores, several points, and the words for not-a-number and infinity.
3. In `read_table` the header row is always read as text, quoted or not; only the data rows are typed. `read_rows` types every row.
4. The writer has to produce what the reader expects. With nonnumeric quoting, booleans are now written unquoted (as the true and false words given to the writer) instead of quoted, like numbers and missing values; text stays quoted, the empty string included. A float that is not finite (not-a-number or either infinity) cannot be read back, so with nonnumeric quoting it raises ValueError; the other quoting modes write it as before. As a result, a table of ints, floats, booleans, text and None written with nonnumeric quoting by `write_table` and read back with nonnumeric quoting by `read_table` equals the original, as long as the same true and false words are used.

All behavior that the existing tests check must keep working.
